source.name: Unrecognized or cleared countries must not save an old code, even when submitted from the field
source.scope: Fourth post-hoc strengthening. Ultra run bea9de3c attempt 2 passed every native-form-submit gate by comparing the visible text with option textContent exactly. A reviewer probe (2026-10-24) reformatted the same options the way server templates commonly print them (text on its own indented line): with that patch, saving without touching either field erased both saved countries, and choosing France saved nothing. The original component kept them. This case uses that semantically identical markup and adds a guard: an untouched save must keep both saved countries. The single-line page is withheld as a transfer check. Pinned GOV.UK component unchanged. Not blind or production-customer evidence.

guards.title: Guard · saving without editing keeps both saved countries
guards.goal: Saving must submit exactly what each country field shows. A listed country submits its code. An empty, blank or unrecognized entry submits no saved country (an empty value). Keyboard and pointer selection of listed countries must keep working.

plan.root_cause: The autocomplete enhancement does not update the underlying select element when the user enters an unrecognized value and submits the form. The form's submit event listener only prevents default but does not synchronize the select elements with the autocomplete inputs, leaving the previously selected country codes intact.
plan.repair_strategy: Update the form's submit event listener to synchronize each enhanced select element with its corresponding autocomplete input. For each input, if its value matches an option's text, select that option; otherwise, select the empty option (value ""). This ensures that unrecognized or cleared entries result in an empty saved country while preserving valid selections made via keyboard or pointer.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: The form will correctly reflect the user's input, including clearing the saved country when the input is unrecognized or empty, while preserving keyboard and pointer selection behavior for valid options.
functional_risks: The synchronization runs on form submit, which may not cover cases where the form is submitted programmatically without the submit event. However, the current UI only uses the save button (type=submit) and Enter key in the form, both triggering the submit event.
verification_requirements: Test that typing an unrecognized country (e.g., "Atlantis") and submitting clears the saved country (empty string).
Test that selecting a valid country via keyboard (arrow keys + Enter) or pointer (click) still saves the correct country code.
Test that clearing the field (empty input) and submitting saves an empty value.
Test that partial matches confirmed on blur (e.g., "Fra" -> France) still save the matched country.

plan.repair_strategy: Update the form's submit event listener to synchronize each enhanced select element with its corresponding autocomplete input. This ensures that unrecognized or cleared entries result in an empty saved country while preserving valid selections made via keyboard or pointer.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: The form will correctly reflect the user's input, including clearing the saved country when the input is unrecognized or empty, while preserving keyboard and pointer selection behavior for valid options. Trimming and case-sensitive matching might cause issues if the autocomplete returns text with different casing or whitespace; we mitigate by trimming both sides.
